data.segment_description:
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced. 
 (Studio: Terry Moran)  President Bush's speech tonight at the Republican National Convention previewed; excerpts quoted; scenes shown of Bush touring the stage in Madison Square Garden this afternoon; details given of his plans to defend his record on Iraq & the economy & explain his goals for a second term, including education, health care & taxes.  [White House communication director Dan BARTLETT†- says the president is excited & will give a substantive speech.]  Bush's plans to campaign in four battleground states tomorrow noted. 
 (Studio: Peter Jennings, George Stephanopoulos)  The overnight reconfiguration of the podium for the Bush speech aimed at the undecided vote noted.

(Studio: Peter Jennings)  The potential damage from Hurricane Frances in Florida introduced. 
 (Miami: Jeffrey Kofman)  The evacuation of Floridians featured; scenes shown of preparedness pandemonium.  [Ft. Lauderdale resident Bradley KVIDDEL†- says the high winds are scary.]  [Miami-Dade County Mayor Alex PENELAS†- calls for evacuation.]  [National Hurricane Center deputy director Ed RAPPAPORT†- predicts a major impact in Florida.] 
 (Studio: Peter Jennings)  Map shown of the hurricane nearing the Bahamas. 
 (Nassau, Bahamas: Bill Blakemore)  The expected arrival of Frances in the Bahamas featured; scenes shown from Nassau of people waiting in line for bottled water.  [Radio talk show host Darryl MILLER†- says we may have underestimated this "monster hurricane."]

(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced.   (Moscow: Jim Sciutto)  The ongoing hostage situation at a school in Beslan, Russia, taken over by Chechen rebels featured; scenes shown from outside the school of the people & Russian security forces; details given of a statement from President Vladimir Putin† about the situation & the overall fear in Moscow of another terrorist attack.

data.segment_description:
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Last night's statements at the Republican National Convention from Vice President Dick Cheney about Senator John Kerry, a war on terror & the U.N. quoted.  [August 5, KERRY&nbsp- says he could fight a more  sensitive war on terror.] 
 (New York: Jake Tapper)  A look at whether last night's criticism of Kerry matched his actual Senate record presented; details given about defense spending views after the Cold War & of Republican claims that Kerry is incapable of defending the country.  [Senator Zell MILLER&nbsp- lists the weapons Kerry opposed in the Senate.]  [Annenberg Political Fact Check Brooks JACKSON†- says Miller chose his words about Kerry on weapons systems carefully.]  [January 28, 1992, President BUSH&nbsp- says we will cut defense spending by 1997.]  [American Enterprise Inst. Norman ORNSTEIN†- says then-Defense Secretary Cheney opposed the same weapons systems.]  [January 31, 1992, CHENEY&nbsp- names the weapons programs we don't need.]  [Last night, CHENEY, MILLER&nbsp- attack Kerry.]

The Money Trail (Convention Campaign Finances) Part IV
data.segment_description: (Convention floor: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced.   (New York: Brian Ross)  Politics & money at the Republican National Convention featured; details given about the charity events like last night's AIDS fund raiser hosted by Senate majority leader Bill Frist, a golf teaching party & the American Council for Excellence in Opportunity, a group linked to Representative Michael Oxley's PAC.  [Africa Action executive director Salih BOOKER†- calls it "deplorable" manipulation of the AIDS issue & giving donors access to power.]  [FRIST&nbsp- says it {the fund raiser} is unrelated to the convention.]  IRS documents linking the AIDS charity to the Republicans detailed.

Campaign 2004 / Bush vs. Kerry / Laura Interview
data.segment_description: (Studio: Peter Jennings)  Excerpts from a taped interview with First Lady Laura Bush presented.  [BUSH&nbsp- says tonight is the big speech; states her husband is the favorite in the presidential election race; comments on the Swift boat ads attacking Senator John Kerry's record; asserts we have a responsibility to be civil in politics.]
